sections.h2: Where to find the Benzie County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Go to Suite 202 of the Government Center, 448 Court Place, Beulah, MI 49617. The counter is staffed weekdays from half past eight in the morning to five in the afternoon, and the phone number is 231-882-0016.

Every deed, mortgage and easement for land in Benzie's townships and in the city of Frankfort lands in the same index at this one counter.

  • Clerks cannot supply blank forms or weigh in on legal questions. People who need a deed written are told to see an attorney or a title company.
  • A filing can arrive over the counter, by post, via UPS or FedEx, or by electronic submission.
  • If you request copies by mail, enclose your own return envelope with postage.

The charge is $30.00 per filing however many pages it runs. Michigan's MCL 600.2567 sets that same $30 and includes the survey fee inside it. If one paper assigns or discharges multiple instruments, each instrument after the first brings a $3.00 surcharge.

Certain papers need a County Treasurer certificate first: warranty deeds, any deed that promises warranty, land contracts and assignments of them, and condominium master deeds. Under MCL 211.135 the proof covers five years of taxes before the instrument date.

Plan the budget in two parts. The recording fee and any $3.00 surcharges go to the Register. The tax certificate goes to the County Treasurer on its own check, and vendor fees for electronic filing are billed by the vendor.

Four vendors handle electronic submissions: Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm. Each sets its own price, and the Register adds nothing more, so the vendor's charge is the only extra cost to budget for.

If your deed also calls for county tax certification, the office recommends ePN because a document router links the two. A single electronic package can then serve both offices.

Searching is its own service. Names are indexed by seller and buyer, and scans reach back to the mid 1800s. The public Tapestry link charges for use, and title professionals may take a Laredo subscription arranged by phone.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Benzie County deed
sections.html:
The office collects state transfer tax as the deed goes on record, and its website links the county act (MCL 207.505) and the state act (MCL 207.526). The state charge is $3.75 on each $500 of price, a partial block rounding up, or $7.50 per $1,000. Call the office to learn the county amount for your instrument. Lakefront prices run high, so the tax deserves a line in any shoreline seller's net sheet.

Some transfers escape the state tax, and the instrument has to say which exemption it claims.

  • A price below $100, loan security papers, leases and mineral interests.
  • A deed passing from a person to a son, daughter, stepchild or grandchild.
  • A court order that sets no dollar price, a boundary adjustment, or a corrective quitclaim.
  • A land contract in which the seller still holds title, and foreclosure deeds, including deeds given to avoid foreclosure.

The office records land related paper, and the list is broad. A seller or an heir will meet several of these during a sale or estate settlement.

  • Warranty, quit claim and mineral deeds, as well as administrator, tax and sheriff's deeds.
  • Mortgages, along with assignments and discharges of them.
  • Liens for state and federal tax, circuit court orders, and probate orders.
  • Certificates of trust, master deeds, rights of way, restrictions and subdivision plats.
  • Surveys, land corner records and remonumentation records.

Payoff paperwork matters most with an older loan. A lender files a discharge once a mortgage is satisfied, and the buyer's closer checks this index for it before title is cleared.

Sequence matters at a small counter. Begin with the title commitment, so you know which liens need a discharge. If the deed has a warranty clause, request the Treasurer's certificate next, or send the deed through ePN so certification travels with it. After that, check that the deed states the complete price, because transfer tax follows the stated price.

Last, choose how it gets there. Carry it in on a weekday, post it with a return envelope, or let the closing agent send it through one of the four vendors. A family transfer should name its exemption right on the instrument, so the tax is not collected in error.

What to bring if you file in person: the signed original deed, a check for the recording fee and transfer tax made out to the Register of Deeds, and a separate check to the County Treasurer if a tax certificate is needed. Ask the clerk to confirm the total before you pay. If the property is an inherited cabin or a family lake house, bring the earlier deed or probate paperwork too, so the index entry can be matched to the right owner.

When the closing is handled by a title company, none of this is your job, but you should still ask which of the four vendors they use and when the recorded deed is expected back. Recording is the point where the sale becomes part of the public record, so a buyer's lender will want proof that it happened.

sections.h2: Other county offices a seller may call
sections.html:
Upstairs in the same building is the Treasurer, at 231-882-0011, on the same weekday schedule. That office administers delinquent tax under Public Act 206 and keeps the tax rolls. Online payments of delinquent tax cost 2.49 percent by card (minimum $1.50) or $1.00 by e-check.

Downstairs, Equalization works from Suite 130 at 231-882-0015. It supplies parcel maps, descriptions, values, sales data, tax maps and millage rates, and it links a parcel search and FEMA map change forms, handy for lakefront owners.

A free Property Fraud Alert service from the Register emails you when any document is recorded under your name, which helps an owner who lives elsewhere catch a forged deed early. The Register also collects the state remonumentation fee as part of each filing, leads the county Plat Board that reviews new subdivisions, and processes U.S. passport applications.

sections.h2: Benzie County housing at a glance
sections.html: Benzie is small and growing, with 18,568 people in 2025, up 3.3 percent from 2020. The county counts 12,682 housing units against only 7,708 households, and 87.8 percent of occupied homes belong to their occupants. The 2020 to 2024 median home value is $285,700. Median gross rent is $1,026 a month, a useful benchmark if the house you are selling has a tenant. Because units outnumber households so widely, ask the title agent early whether any owner or heir lives out of the area, since that changes where papers are signed and mailed.

faqs.q: What is Benzie County's fee for filing a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars a document, no matter how long it is. A paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds three dollars for each one after the first.

faqs.q: Does the Benzie County Register of Deeds add a surcharge for electronic filing?
faqs.a: No. Only the vendor you pick bills a fee, and the approved list is Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm.

faqs.q: When is a tax certificate required in Benzie County?
faqs.a: Warranty deeds, land contracts and condominium master deeds need one. Up to five descriptions cost $5.00, and each further description is 20 cents.

faqs.q: Will Benzie County staff write my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. Staff do not prepare blank documents or give legal advice, so engage an attorney or a title company.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Benzie County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon, in Suite 202 of the Government Center in Beulah. Phone 231-882-0016 first if you have a question.
